question: How raw single-lead ECG becomes a time-ordered sequence of rhythm probabilities through a residual convolutional network.
cannot_conclude: No prospective clinical benefit or autonomous intervention.
No claim that every output sees only its 256-sample interval.

elements.unit: 200 samples/s; voltage unit not reported here

elements.object: two-convolution special first residual block and bypass
15 subsequent residual blocks; preactivation and dropout

observations.whole: Tall signal-to-label composition. One ECG strip at top; small colored operator rectangles; shortcut paths on right; repeated body grouped by dashed enclosure and ×15; output labels along bottom.
observations.critical_detail: First block begins with convolution; repeated body begins BatchNorm/ReLU. Right bypass rejoins after second convolution. Max-pool is drawn in schematic branches, but Methods says only alternating blocks subsample; do not interpret every repeated block as another factor-2 reduction.
observations.graphic_limits: Waveform lacks time/amplitude axis. Crop is detail of ED1, not a second case. Original strip is not transferred or reconstructed as patient data.

source_conflicts.detail: Abstract 53,877 versus explicit training 53,549 and separate test328. Do not label training53549 as all-study total or silently replace figures. New diagram only uses main-test counts.

Methods mentions three groups of112 (336) while final test repeatedly reported328; no reconstruction of exclusions from this inconsistency. New figure uses reported primary test328 and omits per-committee subgroup counts.
